official.description: The Lund University Global Scholarship is a selective, merit-based scholarship programme that each year supports a number of new, high-achieving international students from outside the EU/EEA (and Switzerland) who pay tuition fees. official.program_type: Merit-based tuition fee scholarship for non-EU/EEA fee-paying students
official.english_requirement: English proficiency equivalent to English 6 (advanced level), normally proven by IELTS (Academic) total score 6.5 with no section less than 5.5, or TOEFL internet-based total score 90 with 20 in the written test; previous upper secondary or university studies may also qualify. Some programmes require a higher level, for example English Level 7 - always check the individual programme's admission requirements. The English proficiency deadline is the same as the deadline for supporting documentation.

applicant_utility.summary: This award only reduces tuition, so you must be able to fund every living cost yourself before the Swedish Migration Agency will let you take up the place. The operating window is very short - the scholarship portal opens in early February and closed on 16 February in the last cycle - and it opens only after your national application at universityadmissions.se is complete with the fee paid. Build the plan backwards from that February window: national application and fee first, motivation letter ready, living-cost funds documented.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving non-EU/EEA applicants with strong, consistent academic records who can document their own living-cost funding of roughly SEK 8,900-12,000 per month.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the universityadmissions.se application and pay the application fee well before February, because the scholarship portal only opens to applicants whose national application is already complete
List your Lund programme as your first choice on universityadmissions.se - it is an eligibility rule, not a ranking preference
Draft the 600-word Scholarship Motivation Letter as a separate document from your statement of purpose, addressing both your academic track record and why Lund specifically
Book any English test early and make sure results reach University Admissions in Sweden by the supporting-documents deadline, not by the scholarship deadline
Have a bank statement, sponsor letter or loan documentation ready proving the Swedish Migration Agency's living-cost requirement before admission results arrive
common_rejection_risks: Ranking another university above Lund at universityadmissions.se, which makes the applicant ineligible regardless of grades
Uploading the programme statement of purpose instead of the Scholarship Motivation Letter, or breaching the 600-word limit
Leaving the national application fee unpaid, since the scholarship portal is only open to complete national applicants
Submitting more than one LUGS application in the same round, which is not permitted
Writing a hardship-focused letter - selection is purely merit-based and financial need is not considered
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs of roughly SEK 8,900-12,000 per month according to Lund University's own example budget (food SEK 3,000; accommodation SEK 4,000-8,000; course literature SEK 400-1,000; miscellaneous SEK 1,500), plus the share of tuition not covered by the awarded percentage, the universityadmissions.se application fee, and travel to Sweden.
document_audit: The 600-word Scholarship Motivation Letter is a distinct upload from the statement of purpose - submitting one document for both purposes is a common trap
English test results must reach University Admissions in Sweden by the supporting-documents deadline; sending them only before the scholarship deadline is not enough
Music and Fine Arts applicants (and March-April round applicants) receive different instructions by email, so do not assume the standard portal route applies to you
alerts: The window closes fast: the round opens in early February and the last deadline was 16 February 2026 - start preparation in the autumn
For successful recipients, the remaining tuition instalment can be due earlier than the general tuition deadline stated in the award email
The scholarship alone cannot fund the residence permit - the Swedish Migration Agency living-cost requirement must be met with your own or family funds
You may apply for other scholarships such as the Swedish Institute scholarships in addition to your single LUGS application
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the national application and pay the fee at www.universityadmissions.se, then watch the scholarship page for the portal link in early February and submit the motivation letter there.
